 Ahead of the Nataru and Rainy Season Holidays, the Minister of Transportation Prioritizes Transportation Accident Prevention
 09 November 2026, 17:30 
 Minister of Transportation (Menhub) Dudy Purwagandhi. (Teddy VOI) 
 JAKARTA - The government prioritizes transportation safety ahead of the 2026 Christmas and New Year 2027 (Nataru) holidays, which coincide with the rainy season. Minister of Transportation (Menhub) Dudy Purwagandhi said all modes of transportation must be prepared to reduce the risk of accidents during the holiday period.
 Dudy conveyed this before attending a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto at the Presidential Palace Complex, Jakarta, Monday, November 9.
 "This is about preparing for the end of the year," said Dudy when asked about the agenda of the meeting at the Palace.
 He explained that the discussion included readiness to face Christmas and New Year holidays as well as the rainy season.
 According to Dudy, the Ministry of Transportation will focus on the readiness of all modes of transportation, both land, sea, air, and railways.
 "Yes, the readiness of all modes of transportation. What we prioritize is during Nataru we try or we try to minimize accidents," he said.
 However, Dudy has not detailed the security measures that will be carried out, including vehicle eligibility checks, readiness of transportation facilities, and anticipation of travel disruptions due to bad weather.
 He said the issue would be discussed further with the President.
 "Later we will discuss it with the President," he said.
 Apart from Nataru's preparations, Dudy also received questions regarding the cancellation of PT Kereta Api Indonesia's (Persero) plan to import used electric train cars (KRL) from Japan.
 Dudy admitted that he had not met with KAI President Director Bobby Rasyidin to discuss the issue.
 "I haven't met the CEO of KAI," he said.
 Previously, KAI canceled plans to import used KRL from Japan and chose to procure a new series. The company needs an additional 23 KRL series for Jabodetabek services, with eight of them being urgent needs.
 KAI plans to involve domestic industries, including PT Industri Kereta Api (INKA), as well as opening up opportunities for cooperation with foreign manufacturers.
 When asked when he would meet with the head of KAI to discuss the need for the fleet, Dudy emphasized that the conversation needed to be carried out immediately.
 "Yes, as soon as possible, because we need the train as soon as possible, yes," he said.
